transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-15 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~38m | Attendees: Maya, Liam (Redwood) — Raj, Sofia, Ethan, Carla (Pacifica)

00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
00:03 Raj Patel: yes loud and clear, thanks Maya, we ran a bit over so appreciate you squeezing us in
00:07 Maya Chen: of course, quick agenda — model selection constraints: context length, multilingual support, tool-calling, and deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private). we'll take notes and outline next steps.
00:19 Sofia Alvarez: great, i'll give a quick overview of what we're building — voice assistant for travel planning, multi-lingual (EN/ES/PT/FR), and we need memory across long sessions, so 50k+ tokens maybe — ish. also need to call booking API and internal knowledge tools.
00:36 Liam Ortiz: ok, good context. when you say 50k, are you thinking active KV cache across conversations or single prompt windows?
00:44 Sofia Alvarez: mostly single session context; we want the model to reference earlier parts of the conversation, full itinerary history. could be multi-turn up to 80k in some sessions, but typical 20–40k.
00:56 Ethan Moore: from infra — security is a must. we have SSO, SAML, and strict data residency for EU customers. also prefer KMS integration and audit logs.
01:08 Maya Chen: noted. quick question on throughput and latency — what's acceptable for you on user facing flows?
01:14 Carla Gomez: sub 800ms for short responses ideal, but for longer plan generations we can tolerate 2–3 seconds. cost is also a hard constraint, we're trying to optimize token costs.
01:27 Liam Ortiz: ok, so tradeoffs: big context (32k/100k) usually means larger memory and possibly higher latency, unless you use KV caching or model variants. For model selection, there are open models (Llama derivatives, Mistral, Mosaic/Redpajama variants) and some quantized options. Redwood supports routing between hosted and dedicated.
01:42 Raj Patel: can you explain the hosted vs dedicated vs private implications for model choice?
01:47 Maya Chen: hosted — easiest, pay-as-you-go, continuous improvements; we'd provision higher context models in the catalog (32k variants) and you can test quickly. Dedicated — reserved GPU pools, lower and more consistent latency, better for high throughput and custom quantized models. Private — for strict compliance, full control but heavier ops, you can bring your own model builds and HSM/KMS.
02:05 Sofia Alvarez: and for tool-calling? we need robust function/tool calling (structured outputs, retry semantics). does Redwood's hosted API support that?
02:12 Liam Ortiz: yes, Redwood exposes function-calling primitives and structured output helpers. caveat: some open models don't have native tool-calling affordances so we rely on prompt wrappers and output parsing; other models with instruction tuning are easier. we can also use post-process validators.
02:26 Raj Patel: which models would you recommend for multilingual + long context?
02:29 Liam Ortiz: depends on accuracy vs cost. options we typically discuss: 1) 32k Llama-deriv with instruction tuning — good balance; 2) Mistral-type models (strong multilingual in some versions) — cost-effective; 3) 100k context models (some open checkpoints support longer contexts or you can use Redwood's context windowing + KV cache to emulate longer memory) — higher resource use. we can spin up a few variants in a pilot.
02:52 Sofia Alvarez: are there differences in hallucination tendencies between these? we care about factuality for bookings.
02:58 Liam Ortiz: yes, instruction-tuned and larger context usually reduce hallucinations, but evaluation with your prompts is the only reliable check. our Optimize product can run quality regressions against prompt sets.
03:12 Ethan Moore: from infra — will dedicated let us use GPU types that support 100k contexts without swapping? we need predictable RAM/GPU memory.
03:20 Maya Chen: dedicated gives you reserved capacity and we can recommend instance types for long context. we also provide model compilation and kernel selection tuned to your workload. for true private on-prem with HSM you'd be managing instance types yourself.
03:36 Raj Patel: any compliance concerns with hosted? like EU data residency and logs?
03:40 Maya Chen: hosted can be regionally restricted — EU region available, and we support KMS integrations, but some customers prefer dedicated/private for strict controls. we'll send our SOC2 and security architecture.
03:52 Carla Gomez: pricing — can you ballpark hosted vs dedicated costs for 32k vs 100k contexts?
03:57 Maya Chen: rough: hosted per-token pricing increases with model size; 100k context models are materially more expensive per request. dedicated is priced as reserved capacity — better for sustained throughput. we'll share a detailed comparison spreadsheet after the call.
04:12 Sofia Alvarez: we also need multilingual evals — do you provide eval tooling?
04:16 Liam Ortiz: yes, Redwood Optimize supports evals across prompt sets and languages, can alert regressions, and recommend quantization profiles that preserve quality in other languages.
04:28 Raj Patel: about quantization — does that impact tool-calling or structured outputs?
04:32 Liam Ortiz: sometimes; aggressive quantization can slightly change tokenization behavior or confidence calibration. for structured outputs we usually prefer fp16 or mild quantization and run model-specific tests.
04:45 Sofia Alvarez: ok. can you run a pilot that does: 1) hosted 32k Llama-deriv vs hosted 100k variant, 2) dedicated Mistral-type quantized profile, 3) private deploy baseline? we want latency, cost, multilingual quality, and tool-calling reliability.
04:58 Maya Chen: yes that's feasible. timeline?
05:01 Raj Patel: asap — 2 weeks to get initial benchmarks would be great.
05:04 Liam Ortiz: we can target 10 business days; i'll need your prompt set and sample tools.
05:09 Sofia Alvarez: i'll share prompts and the booking API spec after this — probably by Thursday.
05:13 Maya Chen: perfect. i'll send pricing and security docs; Liam will own the benchmark plan. any blockers?
05:20 Ethan Moore: one more — network egress concerns for hosted EU customers, any mitigations?
05:24 Maya Chen: we can route EU requests to EU region, and for Dedicated/Private you can keep traffic within VPC and use private endpoints.
05:33 Carla Gomez: ok that helps. what about fallback behavior if model overloaded? we need graceful degradation.
05:38 Liam Ortiz: Redwood supports smart routing and fallback to smaller model variants or cached responses to preserve latency SLOs. we'll include suggestions in the benchmark plan.
05:47 Raj Patel: next steps recap please.
05:49 Maya Chen: recap: 1) Maya to send pricing + SOC2/security pack by Friday 6/18; 2) Liam to send benchmark plan and schedule deep dive for running 32k/100k tests by 6/20; 3) Pacifica (Sofia) to send prompt set and booking API by 6/17; 4) schedule pilot kickoff once artifacts received.
06:10 Sofia Alvarez: sounds good, thanks everyone.
06:13 Maya Chen: thanks all.
06:15 End of meeting.
